This app scans Cloudflare's official IP ranges and ranks the addresses that are genuinely usable.

What the numbers mean
"How many IPs to test" is the number of addresses picked at random from Cloudflare's ranges and tested — not the number of clean ones you will end up with.

The number tested can exceed what you asked for: each time a clean IP is found, its neighbouring addresses are tested too, because Cloudflare's servers tend to sit next to one another.

"Clean" means the IP passed every test. The rest were tested and failed, and are not listed.

The four columns on each result
Each measurement has a short label above its value, so the columns stay aligned and no symbol has to be guessed.

"Ping" is the round-trip time to that IP in milliseconds; lower is better.

"Jitter" is how much the ping varies; lower is better. A connection with a high but steady ping beats a fast but erratic one.

"Loss" is the share of data that never arrived. It combines failed attempts with the real figures Cloudflare's own server reports.

"Speed" is megabits per second, measured after the scan on the best results only, a few at a time. A dash means this IP was not among them. ⚠️ Scanning itself only checks that an IP carries real data at all; measuring speed during the scan would time sixteen downloads competing for one radio, which describes the queue rather than the edge.

"Datacenter" is the code of the Cloudflare server that answered you: ⁨VIE⁩ is Vienna, ⁨FRA⁩ Frankfurt, ⁨IST⁩ Istanbul. A nearer datacenter scores higher.

"⁨WebSocket⁩" means the IP accepted a ⁨WebSocket⁩ connection — important for clients such as ⁨VLESS⁩ and ⁨Trojan⁩ that run over it.

How each IP is tested
A ⁨TCP⁩ connection, a ⁨TLS⁩ handshake, confirmation that it really is a Cloudflare server, holding the connection idle to see whether a firewall cuts it, and finally a real data transfer.

Scoring values stability and consistency above raw speed: a steady IP at 250 ms ranks above an unstable one at 30 ms.

Important
Turn your ⁨VPN⁩ off while scanning, or the results describe the tunnel rather than the real network.

Tap a row to copy that one IP. The Copy button copies the whole list in ranked order.

Results are a snapshot — network behaviour shifts constantly, so scan again whenever the IPs stop working.
The app was in the background during part of this scan, so some results may be understated. Rescan for accurate figures.
⚠️ Downloads a fixed amount of real data through each IP and measures its download speed. With a large number of IPs this consumes a significant amount of data. Enable it deliberately.
Runs after the scan on every healthy result. A bigger download measures speed more accurately and counts for more in the score, but uses more data.
Saved in English with all test measurements, whatever the app language
